newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts this week - Downside risk from data deluge.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts this week - Downside risk from data deluge.

text.p: UK gilts face a barrage of domestic data this week, including key May earnings and June PSBR due Wednesday, and the balance of market risk is to the downside, analysts said on Monday.

The market shrugged off the first data release of the week -- weaker-than-expected June producer price inflation figures -- but then shed 15/32 at 114-12/32 on the back of strong selling against Bunds.

"The PPI was the best chance we had of a positive number for the market," said Tom Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale in London. "The figure was OK but didn't give gilts a boost. What lies ahead could be a bit negative."

UK producer output prices fell 0.2 percent in June compared with forecasts of an unchanged figure, reversing a rise of 0.2 percent the previous month. Producer input prices fell by a seasonally adjusted 0.8 percent on the month against a forecast 0.5 percent fall and a rise of 0.6 percent in May.
The next big challenge for gilts will be British Retail Consortium data for June, due for release at 2330 GMT this evening.
HSBC bond economist Don Smith warned that further news of strong spending by consumers would spark further market concerns about the inflationary impact of burgeoning demand.
"It could re-light the burners under the short-end of the curve, depressing the market level and creating renewed impetus for inversion," he said.
Wednesday's May earnings release will also be scrutinised for signs of inflationary pressure from the labour market.

"Wednesday's average earnings figures are a potential acid-test," said Kevin Adams, UK bond strategist at BZW. The robust nature of the UK economy meant the numbers could come in above market expectations of no change from the previous month, he said.
"Average earnings is the indicator likely to draw the most sensitive reaction from the market, because it's the most entrenched form of inflation," Adams said.
Rayner at Societe Generale also said the earnings data could spark concern.
"Signs of wage pressure could push the underlying series up from 4.5 to 4.75 percent, and would be consistent with further rate rises to come," Rayner said.
But while Adams said June PSBR could give rise to reassessment at the long end of the curve, Rayner saw a high PSBR figure having limited impact.
"I think we're going to see a big number, but the market knows there are distortions here," said Rayner.
Rayner cited bunching of gilt coupon payments in June and December and changes to how VAT (value added tax) is accounted for as factors likely to distort the PSBR data.
A Reuter poll forecast June PSBR to rise to 4.1 billion stg from 4.0 billion the previous month.
Wednesday also sees the release of the minutes of the June 5 and 6 monetary meeting -- the Bank of England's first after gaining autonomy for setting interest rates.
"It will be interesting to separate the hawks from the doves, and see if the hawkish members were saying rates needed to move sharply higher," Rayner said.
The Bank raised interest rates by 25 basis points at the June meeting and then again last week, taking them to 6.75 percent.
It cited strong money supply growth as one of the reasons for the rises in interest rates and the release of M4 broad money supply figures on Friday is another source of anxiety for the gilt market.
"The real risk is Friday's M4. The signs are mortgage volumes could be up quite sharply," Rayner said. "We see a strong M4 number around 7.0 billion in June."
Provisional June M4, a broad money supply measure, is forecast to come in at 6.1 billion stg compared with 9.1 billion the previous month.
Rayner said that rate rises factored in by the market could dampen any reaction to a higher M4 figure, but saw most of the coming week's data supporting the need for further interest rate rises.
